source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This Flexential cluster spans Georgia (Alpharetta, Douglasville, Norcross), Florida (Fort Lauderdale, Jacksonville, Tampa), North Carolina (Charlotte, Morrisville), and Tennessee (Brentwood, Franklin), the historic Southeastern United States footprint of Peak 10. According to Flexential own company history page, Peak 10 was founded in 2000 and built a strong regional presence across the Southeastern US. In 2017 Peak 10 purchased ViaWest, merging the two regionally dominant data center providers, and the combined company rebranded as Flexential in 2018. Flexential also acquired AppliedTrust and INetU in 2015 to expand its professional services and cloud offerings. Flexential operates 40 plus data centers across 18 national markets under CEO Ryan Mallory. No building specific address or individual MW figures for these particular registry rows were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Flexential Atlanta - Douglasville 2 in Douglasville, Georgia, publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 358,000 square feet of technical space, operated by Flexential.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 3600 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 900 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

Flexential Atlanta - Douglasville 2 holds 7 published certifications: SOC 1 Type 2 (audited controls over financial reporting processes), SOC 2 Type 2 (audited controls over security, availability, and confidentiality, tested over time rather than at a point), PCI DSS (the standard required to handle payment card data), ITAR (a specific compliance or security standard), NIST 800-53 (alignment with the federal security control catalog), HITRUST (a healthcare-focused security framework built on top of HIPAA). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Georgia has 7 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 4 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 66.3 MW. Flexential Atlanta - Douglasville 2 contributes 36 MW of that total. That is a meaningful facility by colocation standards, though still below the scale where frontier AI training clusters typically operate.
